methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, this meant separating the description of the flip-flops, byte enables, reset, and clock triggering into distinct units. For the generated specification, the header definition, combinational logic functions, enhanced combinational descriptions, and timing logic summaries were parsed to extract individual pieces of information about data updates, reset conditions, and signal behavior.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Byte-enable inputs control whether each byte of the 16 registers should be written to on that cycle
byteena[1] controls the upper byte d[15:8]
byteena[0] controls the lower byte d[7:0]
resetn is a synchronous, active-low reset
All DFFs should be triggered by the positive edge of clk
Create a 16-bit register using D flip-flops
When a byte-enable input is asserted (1), the corresponding byte of the register is updated with the value from the data input 'd' at the rising edge of the clock
When a byte-enable input is deasserted (0), the corresponding byte retains its previous value
When 'resetn' is low at the rising edge of the clock, all 16 flip-flops are reset to 0
spec_atomic_units: Defines a 16-bit register `q` with byte-enable functionality
Inputs are `clk` (clock), `resetn` (active-low synchronous reset), `byteena` (byte enable signals), and `d` (16-bit data input)
`byteena` input controls which byte of the register `q` is updated with the corresponding byte from the input `d`
Lower byte of the output `q[7:0]` is updated with the lower byte of the input `d[7:0]` if `byteena[0]` is asserted (high)
If `byteena[0]` is deasserted (low), the lower byte of `q` retains its previous value
Upper byte of the output `q[15:8]` is updated with the upper byte of the input `d[15:8]` if `byteena[1]` is asserted (high)
If `byteena[1]` is deasserted (low), the upper byte of `q` retains its previous value
The `resetn` input resets the entire register to 0 synchronously with the clock
The output `q` changes only on the positive edge of `clk`
